answer: Assign graders by public randomness, never by choice. Each epoch a beacon seed shuffles every established account into juries, so a farm of 100 keys among 2,000 graders lands on its own answers only about 5% of the time, too rarely to lift its scores. A grader's pay also depends on matching a hidden re-grade of a few sampled seats, so rubber-stamping a garden of clones loses money. A farm may look like a dense nebula of keys, but random seating scatters it, and its horizon of friendly votes shrinks to chance.
